title: Learning Quantum Matter through Attention in Complex Space
authors: Mingrui Jing, Erdong Huang, Jizhe Lai, Enji Xiong, Jin-Guo Liu, Xin Wang
abstract: Magnetic many-electron wavefunctions require amplitude and phase to be optimized together. Whether a complex internal representation improves this variational search is a practical question for neural wavefunction design. We introduce Complex Psiformer for interacting electrons in a magnetic moiré continuum, combining complex hidden features and Hermitian-magnitude attention with magnetic boundary conditions and fermionic antisymmetry. After the same number of optimization steps, Complex Psiformer reaches lower energies than Real Psiformer in two finite supercells. Both Psiformers also improve on their respective neural Hartree-Fock references. Across five training seeds in the 25-cell system, the mean Complex advantage is 1.458 meV per electron, with a smaller observed spread. A separately trained two-electron Complex state has a smaller energy gap to a finite configuration interaction reference than its Real counterpart. In the Complex states, flux scans show nonmonotonic density correlations and weaker honeycomb mean-density modulation at higher flux, while connected fluctuations persist. Gauge invariant current maps provide a qualitative comparison of local circulation in the optimized states. These benchmarks support the combined architecture as a variational ansatz for studying energies and charge arrangements in finite magnetic systems.
summary: This paper proposes Complex Psiformer, a novel neural network ansatz that uses complex-valued features and attention mechanisms to accurately model the wavefunctions of interacting electrons in magnetic moiré superlattices. By incorporating complex phases and magnetic boundary conditions, the model significantly outperforms its real-valued counterpart in minimizing the system's energy. This work establishes a robust variational tool for studying charge order and electronic structure in finite magnetic quantum materials.
main_problem: Developing an effective variational search method for magnetic many-electron wavefunctions, which requires optimizing both amplitude and phase due to strong electronic correlations.
main_result: The Complex Psiformer architecture achieves lower ground state energies compared to its real-valued counterpart, demonstrating the advantage of complex representations for describing correlated electron states in magnetic moiré systems.
method: The authors introduce Complex Psiformer, a neural network architecture that incorporates complex hidden features and Hermitian-magnitude attention (HMCVA) to construct the many-electron wavefunction.
model_or_system: The study focuses on interacting two-dimensional electron gas systems placed in a triangular moiré potential under a perpendicular magnetic field. The Hamiltonian includes kinetic, moiré potential, and electron-electron interaction terms, subject to magnetic boundary conditions.
key_observables: Ground state energy, charge order structure factors ($S(K)$), sublattice occupation patterns ($f_3$), and gauge-invariant current maps.
important_parameters: Magnetic flux quanta ($n_\phi$), system size (e.g., 25-cell supercell), and the comparison between complex and real network representations.
main_assumptions: The method assumes that organizing hidden electron features as complex amplitudes provides necessary radial nonlinearities and Hermitian overlaps for accurate variational optimization.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the moiré geometry, the comparison between Complex Psiformer and Real Psiformer architectures, and the dependence of density anisotropy on training seeds.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the physical model (interacting electrons in a moiré lattice with magnetic flux). It then details the advanced neural network architectures (Complex Psiformer vs. Real Psiformer) designed to handle complex phases and magnetic boundary conditions. Finally, it presents benchmarks comparing the energy and structural properties derived from both complex and real ansatzes.
why_interesting: The explicit handling of complex phases and magnetic boundary conditions within a neural network framework provides a powerful, modern tool for simulating complex quantum phases relevant to condensed matter physics, bridging ML and strongly correlated systems.

Figure 2. Construction of the two complex-valued neural wavefunctions. Complex SlaterNet applies the same one-body network independently to each electron. Complex Psiformer inserts HMCVA before every residual feed-forward layer. This allows each electron representation to incorporate information from the others before the orbital readout and Slater determi- nant. Both models use the same fixed functions at the orbital readout to enforce the magnetic boundary condition. These functions are omitted from the schematic.

Figure 3. Variational-energy optimization over the same num- ber of steps. Panels (a) and (b) show the 18- and 25-cell systems, respectively, both with N = 12 and nϕ = 2. Solid blue and orange curves show the Real and Complex Psiformer training diagnostics. Dashed blue and orange lines indi- cate the corresponding Real and Complex single-determinant SlaterNet neural HF baselines. Table I reports the conven- tional local-energy comparison. The independent Psiformer estimates discussed in the text use the magnetic quadratic- form protocol in Appendix E.
